issues.failure_explanation:
In the proof of Lemma B.2, the transition to the final inequality replaces $\|
abla\ell(	heta_k) - 
abla_	heta \ell_{i,j}(	heta^{(k+1)}_{q-1})\|^2$ with $L^2 \|	heta_k - 	heta^{(k+1)}_{q-1}\|^2$. This invalidly equates the full gradient $
abla\ell(	heta_k)$ with the single pairwise gradient $
abla_	heta \ell_{i,j}(	heta_k)$, which only holds under zero gradient variance across particle pairs. Under non-zero variance $\sigma > 0$ (Assumption A.3), $\|
abla\ell(	heta_k) - 
abla_	heta \ell_{i,j}(	heta_k)\|^2$ does not vanish. Dropping this variance allows Lemma B.2 to falsely claim a deterministic per-epoch descent guarantee for SGD with random reshuffling. Furthermore, Algorithm 2 only evaluates intra-batch pairs $(i,j) \in C_q 	imes C_q$, omitting cross-batch interactions, so the batch updates do not sum to $N B 
abla\ell(	heta_k)$ even in expectation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must correctly incorporate the stochastic variance of the mini-batch gradients under random reshuffling, address the bias resulting from omitting cross-batch particle pairs in Algorithm 2, and establish a valid expected descent inequality.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma B.2 is mathematically false, which directly invalidates Theorem 4.1 (the primary convergence theorem for the optimization method in Algorithm 2). The convergence guarantee of the neural network training scheme is unsupported.
issues.title: Invalid gradient descent bound omitting stochastic gradient variance in Lemma B.2
issues.why_classification: Theorem 4.1 is the sole theoretical convergence guarantee for the paper's stochastic optimization algorithm. Repairing it requires an entirely new proof architecture for random reshuffling on double-sum interaction objectives and resolving the estimator bias in Algorithm 2.
